              type: [32m'text'[39m,
              text: [32m'# Kanban Board with Fractional Ordering (Wasp)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Background\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Build a full-stack Kanban board application with the Wasp framework using the TypeScript spec (`main.wasp.ts`, `wasp: { version: "^0.24.0" }`). The board is made of columns (statuses) and cards. Cards can be moved within a column and across columns. Ordering is stored as a fractional floating-point `position`, so moving a card only ever updates that single card\'s `position` and never renumbers its siblings.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The app uses username & password authentication, a SQLite database (the Wasp development default), Prisma for the data model, and Wasp Operations for the API. All board data is private to the authenticated user who owns it.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Data model (`schema.prisma`):\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `Column`: `id` (Int, primary key), `title` (String), `position` (Float), and an owner relation to `User`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `Card`: `id` (Int, primary key), `title` (String), `position` (Float), a relation to its `Column` exposed through a `columnId` (Int) foreign key, and an owner relation to `User`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * The `User` entity required by Wasp auth.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Enable username & password authentication. Every operation below must act only on data owned by the currently authenticated user.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Implement the following Wasp Operations. The operation names must match exactly (Wasp derives the HTTP route from the name):\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Query `getBoard`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Action `createColumn`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Action `createCard`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Action `moveCard`\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Provide a root route `/` that renders an authenticated page displaying the board and performing an optimistic move (see the optimistic-update requirement below).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Project path: /home/user/kanban\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Start command (run from the project path): `wasp start`\n'[39m +
                [32m'* The Wasp server listens on port 3001; the web client listens on port 3000.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Wasp exposes every Operation as an HTTP `POST` endpoint on the server at `/operations/<kebab-case-operation-name>`. Authenticated calls send an `Authorization: Bearer <sessionId>` header. The relevant endpoints are therefore:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `POST http://localhost:3001/operations/get-board`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `POST http://localhost:3001/operations/create-column`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `POST http://localhost:3001/operations/create-card`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `POST http://localhost:3001/operations/move-card`\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Username authentication endpoints (no session required): `POST http://localhost:3001/auth/username/signup` and `POST http://localhost:3001/auth/username/login`, each accepting a JSON body `{ "username": string, "password": string }`; a successful login responds with a JSON body containing a `sessionId` string.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Any of the four operations invoked without a valid session must fail with `HttpError` status `401`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* `getBoard` (no payload) returns the current user's board as a JSON array of column objects ordered by `position` ascending. Each column object must contain at least the keys `id`, `title`, `position`, and `cards`, where `cards` is an array of that column's cards ordered by `position` ascending. Each card object must contain at least the keys `id`, `title`, `position`, and `columnId`.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* `createColumn` (payload keys: `title` string, `position` number) creates a column owned by the current user at the given position and returns the created column object including `id`, `title`, `position`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `createCard` (payload keys: `title` string, `columnId` number, `position` number) creates a card with the given title and position inside the column identified by `columnId`, and returns the created card object including `id`, `title`, `position`, `columnId`. If `columnId` does not identify a column owned by the current user, the call must fail with `HttpError` status `403` or `404`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* `moveCard` (payload keys: `cardId` number, `targetColumnId` number, `afterCardId` number optional, `beforeCardId` number optional) moves the card identified by `cardId` into the column identified by `targetColumnId` and assigns it a new fractional `position` according to the rules below. It updates only the moved card: the card's `columnId` becomes `targetColumnId` and its `position` is recomputed. No other card's `position` may change. It returns the updated card object including `id`, `title`, `position`, `columnId`. `moveCard` does not accept a caller-supplied position; the server computes it.\n"[39m +
                [32m'  * `afterCardId`, when provided, identifies the card that must end up immediately before the moved card (i.e. with a strictly smaller `position`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `beforeCardId`, when provided, identifies the card that must end up immediately after the moved card (i.e. with a strictly larger `position`).\n'[39m +
                [32m"  * When both `afterCardId` and `beforeCardId` are provided, the moved card's new `position` must equal exactly the arithmetic mean of those two neighbors' `position` values.\n"[39m +
                [32m"  * When only `afterCardId` is provided, the moved card is placed at the tail of the target column: its new `position` must be strictly greater than that neighbor's `position`.\n"[39m +
                [32m"  * When only `beforeCardId` is provided, the moved card is placed at the head of the target column: its new `position` must be strictly smaller than that neighbor's `position`.\n"[39m +
                [32m'  * When neither neighbor is provided, the moved card is the only ordering reference in the target column and may take any valid `position`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `cardId` and `targetColumnId` must identify a card and a column owned by the current user. `afterCardId` and `beforeCardId`, when provided, must identify cards that currently belong to the target column and are owned by the current user. Any violation (a missing resource, or a resource owned by another user) must fail with `HttpError` status `403` or `404`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* The authenticated page at `/` must move a card optimistically: when a move is triggered from the UI, the cached result of the `getBoard` query must be updated to reflect the card's new column and ordering before the server confirms the change, using Wasp's client-side action optimistic-update mechanism for the `moveCard` action."[39m

                    [32m'    version: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Authentication configuration and lifecycle hooks.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * See the [Auth overview](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/overview) for the\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * supported auth methods and how the `User` entity is connected to auth.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * If hooks are async, Wasp awaits them. All hooks receive `prisma` and `req`\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * in their input. Hook return values are ignored except for\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * {@link AuthHooks.onBeforeOAuthRedirect}, which can change the redirect URL.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * In TypeScript, you can type each hook implementation with its matching\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * type from `wasp/server/auth` (e.g. `OnBeforeSignupHook`). See\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [Auth Hooks](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/auth-hooks) for the full hook\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * inputs and examples.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @example\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```ts\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * export default app({\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   // ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   auth: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     userEntity: "User",\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     methods: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *       usernameAndPassword: {}, // use this or email, not both\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *       google: {},\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *       gitHub: {},\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     },\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login",\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   },\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * })\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export interface Auth extends AuthHooks {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Name of the Prisma model that represents the application user connected to\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * your business logic.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * The user entity needs to have an ID field that uniquely identifies each\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * user. It can be of any name and type, but it needs to be marked with `@id`:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * model User {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   id Int @id @default(autoincrement())\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * You can add any other fields you want to the user entity. Make sure to also\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * define them in the `userSignupFields` field if they need to be set during\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * the sign-up process.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Accessing User Data](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/entities) for how the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * user entity connects to the rest of the auth system.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    userEntity: EntityName;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** Enabled authentication methods. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    methods: AuthMethods;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Route that Wasp redirects unauthenticated users to when they try to\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * access a page that has `authRequired: true`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Adding Auth to the Project](https://wasp.sh/docs/tutorial/auth#adding-auth-to-the-project)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * for an example.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAuthFailedRedirectTo: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Route that Wasp redirects users to after a successful login or signup.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m"     * Only takes effect when using Wasp's built-in Auth UI.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Auth UI](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/ui).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @default "/"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAuthSucceededRedirectTo?: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'interface AuthHooks {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called before the user is created. Receives `providerId` plus the common\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * hook input. Throw from this hook to reject a signup based on custom\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * criteria.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onBeforeSignup?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called after the user is created. Receives `providerId`, the created\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * `user`, and, for social auth, `oauth` fields including tokens and the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * unique OAuth request ID.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAfterSignup?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** Called once, after the user verifies their email. Receives `email` and `user`. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAfterEmailVerified?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called before redirecting the user to the OAuth provider. Receives the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * generated `url` and `oauth.uniqueRequestId`. Return `{ url }` to override\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * the redirect URL.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onBeforeOAuthRedirect?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called before the user is logged in. Receives `providerId` and `user`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Throw from this hook to reject a login based on custom criteria.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onBeforeLogin?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called after a successful login. Receives `providerId`, `user`, and, for'[39m,
                  isTruncated: [33mfalse[39m
                }
              },
              providerOptions: {

                    [32m'     * the router will work correctly, and all the assets will be served from'[39m,
                  isTruncated: [33mfalse[39m

                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export interface WebSocket {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Function that registers Socket.IO event handlers. Wasp calls it once on\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * server start with the Socket.IO server instance and a context containing\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * all app entities. If a connected socket is authenticated, Wasp stores the\n'[39m +

                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +

                    [32m'     * If `true` (the default), the client connects to the WebSocket server as\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * soon as the app loads. Set to `false` to connect manually via\n'[39m +

                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    autoConnect?: boolean;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * A single {@link SpecElement}, or an (optionally nested) array of them, that\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * makes up the {@link App.spec}.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * This lets you define related elements separately (for example, one array per\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * feature) and compose them together. The nested structure is treated as a single\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * flat list of elements.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @category Specifications\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @example\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Nested arrays let you compose a spec from separate sub-specs:\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```ts\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * const authSpec: Spec = [signupRoute, loginRoute];\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * const tasksSpec: Spec = [tasksRoute, getTasks, createTask];\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * export default app({\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   // ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   spec: [authSpec, tasksSpec],\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * });\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export type Spec = SpecElement | Spec[];\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Union of every kind of specification element that can appear in {@link App.spec}.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Each variant is produced by its matching constructor.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @category Specifications\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export type SpecElement = Page | Route | Query | Action | Api | ApiNamespace | Job | Crud;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * A page in the app, normally a React component rendered for a {@link Route}.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Create one with the {@link page} constructor.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @category Specifications\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export interface Page extends BaseSpecElement<"page"> {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** React component rendered for this page. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    component: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * If `true`, only authenticated users can access this page. Unauthenticated\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * visitors are redirected to {@link Auth.onAuthFailedRedirectTo}.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Cannot be combined with {@link Route.prerender}.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @default false\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    authRequired?: boolean;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * A URL path mapped to a {@link Page}.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Create one with the {@link route} constructor.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * See [Routing](https://wasp.sh/docs/advanced/routing) for path patterns\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * (dynamic segments, optional segments, splats).\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @category Specifications\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export interface Route extends BaseSpecElement<"route"> {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** Unique route name. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    name: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * URL path. Supports React Router patterns like `/tasks/:id`,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * `/photo/:id/edit?`, and `/files/*`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    path: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** Page rendered when this route matches. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    page: Page;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Render this route to static HTML at build time. Useful for SEO and AI\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * crawlers. The page then hydrates on the client for full interactivity.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Accepts either:\n'[39m +
                    [32m"     * - `true` — prerender this route's own path. The path must be fully static\n"[39m +
                    [32m'     *   (no `:paramName`, `*`, or `?` segments).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * - an array of concrete paths to prerender. Use this to prerender specific\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   instances of a dynamic route (e.g. `["/blog/intro", "/blog/changelog"]`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   for a `"/blog/:slug"` route). Every listed path must be fully static and\n'[39m +
                    [32m"     *   must match this route's path pattern.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m"     * In either case the route's page cannot have {@link Page.authRequired} set,\n"[39m +
                    [32m"     * since prerendered content can't depend on the logged-in user. See\n"[39m +
                    [32m'     * [Prerendering](https://wasp.sh/docs/advanced/prerendering).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @default false\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @example\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```ts\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * import { app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * import { LandingPage } from "./src/LandingPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * import { BlogPostPage } from "./src/BlogPostPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * export default app({\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   // ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   spec: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *     route("LandingRoute", "/", page(LandingPage), {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *       prerender: true,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *     }),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *     route("BlogPostRoute", "/blog/:slug", page(BlogPostPage), {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *       prerender: ["/blog/intro", "/blog/changelog"],\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *     }),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   ],\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * })\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    prerender?: boolean | readonly string[];\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m"     * Lazy-load the page's component.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Set to `false` to include the page in the initial client bundle, which\n'[39m +

                  [32m'    title: column.title,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    position: column.position,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'type CreateCardArgs = {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  title: string;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  columnId: number;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  position: number;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'export const createCard: CreateCard<CreateCardArgs, any> = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (!context.user) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    throw new HttpError(401, "Unauthorized");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (typeof args.title !== "string" || typeof args.columnId !== "number" || typeof args.position !== "number") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    throw new HttpError(400, "Invalid arguments");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // Verify column ownership\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const column = await context.entities.Column.findUnique({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where: { id: args.columnId },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (!column || column.userId !== context.user.id) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    throw new HttpError(403, "Forbidden");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const card = await context.entities.Card.create({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    data: {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      title: args.title,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      position: args.position,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      column: {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        connect: { id: args.columnId },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      user: {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        connect: { id: context.user.id },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  return {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    id: card.id,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    title: card.title,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    position: card.position,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    columnId: card.columnId,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'type MoveCardArgs = {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  cardId: number;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  targetColumnId: number;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  afterCardId?: number;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  beforeCardId?: number;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'export const moveCard: MoveCard<MoveCardArgs, any> = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (!context.user) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    throw new HttpError(401, "Unauthorized");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const { cardId, targetColumnId, afterCardId, beforeCardId } = args;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (typeof cardId !== "number" || typeof targetColumnId !== "number") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    throw new HttpError(400, "Invalid arguments");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 1. Verify target column exists and is owned by the current user\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const column = await context.entities.Column.findUnique({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where: { id: targetColumnId },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (!column || column.userId !== context.user.id) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    throw new HttpError(403, "Forbidden");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 2. Verify card exists and is owned by the current user\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const card = await context.entities.Card.findUnique({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where: { id: cardId },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (!card || card.userId !== context.user.id) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    throw new HttpError(403, "Forbidden");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 3. Verify afterCardId and beforeCardId if provided\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  let afterCard = null;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (afterCardId !== undefined && afterCardId !== null) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    afterCard = await context.entities.Card.findUnique({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      where: { id: afterCardId },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if (!afterCard || afterCard.userId !== context.user.id || afterCard.columnId !== targetColumnId) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      throw new HttpError(403, "Forbidden");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  let beforeCard = null;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (beforeCardId !== undefined && beforeCardId !== null) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    beforeCard = await context.entities.Card.findUnique({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      where: { id: beforeCardId },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if (!beforeCard || beforeCard.userId !== context.user.id || beforeCard.columnId !== targetColumnId) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      throw new HttpError(403, "Forbidden");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 4. Compute new position\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  let newPosition: number;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (afterCard && beforeCard) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    newPosition = (afterCard.position + beforeCard.position) / 2.0;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } else if (afterCard) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    newPosition = afterCard.position + 1.0;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } else if (beforeCard) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    newPosition = beforeCard.position - 1.0;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } else {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    newPosition = 1.0;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 5. Update the card\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const updatedCard = await context.entities.Card.update({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where: { id: cardId },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    data: {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      columnId: targetColumnId,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      position: newPosition,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  return {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    id: updatedCard.id,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    title: updatedCard.title,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    position: updatedCard.position,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    columnId: updatedCard.columnId,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'};\n'[39m +
                  [32m''[39m

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.             [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
